interactables.name: council notice
text: Nailed to the lamp post: by order of the council, bread at the granary gate, one loaf a household, at noon. Nobody is to cross the ford. H. Varrow, Mayor.
Under it, in another hand: "Ask the Marrowbys where their grain went."

interactables.name: square well
text: The bucket comes up warm. The old folk swear this well used to steam in winter.
It doesn't now.

interactables.name: hearthstone
text: A hearthstone of the Church of the Hearth, out on the green where the town buries its own. Someone keeps it swept.
You lay a hand on it. For a moment the cold goes out of your fingers.

interactables.name: Coll's grave
text: COLL. GUARD OF EMBERWICK. HE HELD THE BRIDGE END.
The stone is new, and the earth is still soft.

interactables.name: Annet's grave
text: ANNET. GUARD OF EMBERWICK.
Someone has left a heel of bread on the stone, and a guard's whistle.

interactables.name: signpost
text: East: the Ford Bridge. North: the Skarrow Hills. West: Emberwick.
Somebody has scratched out "Bridge" and cut "TOLL" into the wood.

interactables.name: grain crate
text: Empty. The straw at the bottom smells of last year's wheat.

interactables.name: split sack
text: Seed corn, and a slit in the side where somebody has been helping themselves.

interactables.name: rain barrel
text: Rainwater, with a skin of ice on it. There was never ice in Emberwick.

interactables.name: market crate
text: Turnips, mostly. Small ones.

interactables.name: pier crate

text: A cord pulls taut and a bell rattles somewhere up the pier. Nobody comes. Nobody here ever does.
Packing straw and a smell of hot stone. Whatever was in here has gone.

interactables.name: fish barrel
text: Salt and the last of the summer's eels. The river's too warm for them now, the fishers say.

interactables.name: tally scrap
text: First night: two shards, small. Second night: none, the water's too hot. Third night: one, and Gus burned his hand.
Tell the lady the price goes up.

interactables.name: scuffed boards
text: Boot scuffs in the ash, all heading the same way and stopping at nothing in particular.
